candidates.title: Ford responds to Trump's renaming effort with Lake Ontario 'Now and Always' sign
candidates.description: Ontario Premier Doug Ford unveiled a Lake Ontario sign in Winona Saturday, after United States President Donald Trump signed an executive order to change the name to "Lake America" amid deteriorating relations.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: 'What do they have their hands on?' Customer reacts to Eastlink breach
candidates.description: Telecommunications provider Eastlink is warning some customers of a potential data breach that happened in recent days, but it does not believe that credit card or banking information was exposed. The company operates in seven Canadian provinces and Bermuda.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: An island mysteriously appeared — then disappeared — on B.C.'s largest reservoir
candidates.description: B.C. Hydro says it's monitoring for the reappearance of a mysterious island first spotted by boaters 100 kilometres from the W.A.C. Bennett Dam in northeastern B.C.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Ottawa couple's 'Lake Ontario' hats selling like hotcakes after Trump's executive order
candidates.description: Before the ink had even dried on U.S. President Donald Trump's executive order to rename Lake Ontario, a Canadian company was already selling hats with the Great Lake's true name emblazoned on it.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Canada's Sophia Jensen wins gold at canoe sprint world championships in Poland
candidates.description: Canada's Sophia Jensen won the first world title of her career on Saturday at the 2026 ICF Canoe Sprint & Paracanoe World Championships in Poznań, Poland.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Canada's Danielle Dorris swims to silver in women's butterfly S5-7 at Para Pan Pacific Championships
candidates.description: Two-time Paralympic champion Danielle Dorris of Moncton, N.B., earned Canada's first medal to open the three-day Pan Pacific Swimming Championships, grabbing silver in the women's 50-metre butterfly S5-7 final on Friday night in Walnut, Calif.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Why this Sask. judge provided eagle feathers for the province's courtrooms
candidates.description: Judge Michelle Brass says the meaning of eagle feathers varies between Indigenous communities, and it's especially important for Saulteaux people such as herself.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Junior hockey players in OHL, WHL can seek compensation for alleged abuse, court says
candidates.description: The Ontario Superior Court of Justice has approved an opt-in process for current and former players in the Ontario Hockey League and Western Hockey League who allege they were victims of abuse or hazing.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Ontario's top court sides with lower court, rejects developer's challenge over Greenbelt land
candidates.description: The Ontario Court of Appeal has sided with a lower court in rejecting a developer's constitutional challenge of a 2023 law that returned 15 parcels of land to the Greenbelt.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Sask. Police Commission hears appeal of officer fired for friendship with Hells Angels associate
candidates.description: Former sergeant Robbie Taylor seeks reinstatement with the Saskatoon Police Service, arguing there was an abuse of process during his original hearing.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: 'Suspicious' OSAP activity at some career colleges flagged to province, documents show
candidates.description: The association representing career colleges in Ontario began warning the government about possible "suspicious" student financial aid activity at a few campuses three years ago, documents show.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: 'Canada’s longest serving councillor' is retiring. A new book highlights his 49 years of service in Niagara
candidates.description: A fixture on St. Catharines’, Ont., council for nearly five decades, Joseph Kushner has announced he will be retiring at the upcoming municipal election. A new edition of his biography recounts his life story.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Churchill River power agreement 'absolutely not' like '69, says N.L. Hydro CEO
candidates.description: Newfoundland and Labrador Hydro CEO Jennifer Williams says early increases to Churchill Falls electricity prices, more power for Labrador and less risk in approach to export sales, are all features of the new agreement on Churchill River power.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Unlocking a 400-year-old mystery in a Nova Scotia marsh
candidates.description: On a river in southwest Nova Scotia, an investigation by a historical sleuth is uncovering long-lost traces of North America’s past.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: 'Lake America'? Trump's 'utterly ridiculous' renaming met with laughter in Kingston
candidates.description: The mayor of Kingston, Ont., says a snicker is the only response Donald Trump will be getting from his community following the U.S. president's renaming of Lake Ontario as Lake America. "The best thing we can possibly do is just ignore the silliness," Bryan Paterson says.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Nova Scotians wait over 500 ‘painful’ days for surgery consultations
candidates.description: When the consultation and surgery wait times are combined, the total waits for hip and knee replacements in Nova Scotia are longer than they were a decade ago. In 2015, Nova Scotians could expect a total median wait of 265 days for a hip replacement — in 2025, it was 292 days.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Where do young people stand in separation debates in Alberta and Quebec?
candidates.description: In two Canadian provinces, two different conversations are unfolding about the prospect of leaving the country for good, and it seems two different age cohorts are making the push.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Air Canada will now allow you up to 3 mobility aids on flights in expanded policy
candidates.description: Air Canada announced an expanded mobility aid policy Friday that will allow customers to bring up to three mobility aids free of charge.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Interprovincial trade barriers are falling. But rewriting old rules will take time
candidates.description: The collapse of talks with the United States has added urgency to reducing trade barriers within Canada. But experts say it's not a simple fix.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Treaty 6 was signed 150 years ago. First Nations worry a push for Alberta independence puts it at risk
candidates.description: First Nations from across Treaty 6 territory have been marking this month’s 150th anniversary of the signing of the 1876 agreement with the Crown. But for some, the discussion around the upcoming referendum on Alberta independence is casting a shadow over it.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Rescuers search for thousands following deadly Nepal-China flood
candidates.description: As rescue efforts in communities buried by catastrophic flash floods along the border between Nepal and China entered their fourth day on Saturday, authorities continued finding survivors and transporting them to safety. The death toll and the number of people unaccounted for continued to rise.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: As insults fly around trade, negotiators for Canada and the U.S. avoid getting personal in public
candidates.description: Politicians from Canada and the U.S. have thrown varying degrees of personal insults back and forth across the border this week, but the two governments' trade negotiators avoided getting personal — at least in public. Experts believe the two trade leads are striking a different tone because they have a different role to play as the dispute heats up.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Trump administration video showing Haitian deportees in chains sparks outrage
candidates.description: A U.S. Department of Homeland Security video shows men, handcuffed and in chains, boarding a deportation flight to Haiti this week. Critics say the Trump administration is "bragging" about sending Haitian immigrants "back to a war-torn country" after rescinding temporary protected status.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Israeli settlers attack home in occupied West Bank's Qusra: witnesses
candidates.description: Dozens of masked Israeli settler militants attacked homes surrounding the occupied West Bank village of Qusra on Saturday, the first major attack since a siege by settlers in the area earlier this month drew an international outcry. The settlers surrounded a Palestinian home, throwing stones while seven Palestinians were trapped inside, according to witnesses.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Russian attack on Kyiv region kills at least 37
candidates.description: At least 27 people have been killed following a Russian attack on the Bucha district, close to the Ukrainian capital Kyiv, officials said Saturday.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Iceland votes on whether to start EU membership talks in shadow of Trump's Greenland threats
candidates.description: About 265,000 Icelanders are eligible to vote in a referendum on whether to trigger European Union membership talks. Supporters say membership could offer stability and protection against possible threats from U.S. President Donald Trump, while opponents say it's unnecessary and could endanger rich fishing stocks.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: In Ohio, Canada-U.S. trade war sparks anger and uncertainty
candidates.description: Youngstown, Ohio, sits in a wider congressional district known as OH-6, which exports more than $820 million US in goods to Canada every year. While not all of its imports and exports are caught in the crosshairs of the escalating U.S-Canadian tariffs, a prolonged trade war could threaten some businesses in those sectors.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Trump says U.S. makes deal to control 65 billion barrels of Venezuelan oil reserves
candidates.description: U.S. President Donald Trump said Friday that his administration has entered a sweeping agreement with Venezuela that, if realized, could give the U.S. access to vast amounts of the South American country's untapped oil reserves, at cost.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: What the CIA director’s mystery trip to Moscow says about Putin's next move
candidates.description: An unannounced but highly visible flight to Moscow by CIA Director John Ratcliffe aboard a U.S. Air Force transport plane this week has ignited a fierce debate over Vladimir Putin’s next military move. With Russia’s volunteer recruitment drying up and its economy straining under the weight of 1.4 million casualties, intelligence briefs suggest Putin is preparing a massive, unpopular mobilization of 600,000 new troops.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: U.S. may seek win with Mexico in wake of collapsed trade talks with Canada, says ex-negotiator
candidates.description: The collapse of trade talks between Ottawa and Washington could see U.S. negotiators try to "aggressively" secure a win with Mexico in their ongoing bilateral talks, says a former Mexican trade negotiator.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Iran war hits 6-month milestone with Trump's attention largely elsewhere
candidates.description: A number of U.S. lawmakers called on Donald Trump to end the war with Iran as it reached its six-month mark on Friday, while the U.S. president has given mixed signals regarding the state of the conflict.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: More U.S. rate hikes possible with inflation still elevated, Federal Reserve chair Kevin Warsh says
candidates.description: U.S. Federal Reserve chair Kevin Warsh said Friday that inflation is still too high and suggested the country's central bank may have to raise interest rates in the coming months to bring it down.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Syrian president names former commander of Kurdish-led fighting force as adviser
candidates.description: Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa appointed the former commander of a now-dissolved Kurdish-led fighting force as a presidential adviser on Friday, reflecting a rapprochement between the two longtime civil war adversaries.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: ICE to purchase thousands of electric-shock gloves
candidates.description: U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement has awarded a $16.7 million contract to purchase 6,000 pairs of gloves that can deliver painful electric shocks, saying officers would use them to control detainees and protesters who resist.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: King Harald V, Norway's reform-minded head of state, dead at 89
candidates.description: Norway's King ‌Harald, a ​reformer who emerged ​from the shadow ​of his well-loved ‌father over more than three decades on the ‌throne, has died aged ​89, the royal palace said on ​Friday.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: How teen accounts on Instagram and Facebook are changing after Meta's $18B US settlement
candidates.description: Changes are coming for teen Instagram and Facebook users after parent company Meta agreed to platform changes in a landmark U.S. settlement to resolve claims of online harms to youth. Experts tell CBC News what's changing, how widely and what impact this might have going forward.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Despite Trump's renaming of Lake Ontario, Great Lakes endure as symbol of U.S.-Canada collaboration
candidates.description: It's unclear whether Trump can unilaterally rename the lake, whose name predates European colonization of the Americas and has been widely recognized internationally for centuries. But the renaming belies a concerted push by the Trump administration to hold back important U.S.-Canada collaboration on scientific research and restoration work in the Great Lakes.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Russia hammers Ukrainian ports, warehouses and industrial sites with missiles and drones
candidates.description: Russia ‌hammered Ukrainian ports, industrial sites and retailers' distribution facilities with missiles and drones in an hours-long attack on Kyiv and other cities that was partly repelled, Ukrainian officials said on Thursday.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Old soup factory takes on new high-tech life as quantum computing firm gets $195M federal boost
candidates.description: In the echoey void of a gutted Campbell's Soup factory in Toronto’s west end, Canada's minister of artificial intelligence and digital innovation announced the federal government’s biggest bet to date on homegrown technology that could revolutionize artificial intelligence, medical science and a host of other key sectors of the economy.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Canada's economy has found its footing. But is it enough to survive the U.S. trade war?
candidates.description: GDP growth surged in the spring. Exports, business investment and household spending showed how Canada can weather the trade war storm. The question is whether it can last.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Canada's economy grew a strong 3.3% annualized in 2nd quarter, as 1st quarter revised higher
candidates.description: Canada's economy posted strong growth in the second quarter, driven by high exports and domestic investments. After a slight decline in GDP growth in the first quarter led to fears of a technical recession, an upwards revision of those figures puts those notions in the "trash bin," according to one economist.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: 'Measured confidence': RBC, TD Bank, CIBC share optimistic outlook for Canada's economy
candidates.description: Three of Canada's big banks shared cautiously sunny outlooks for the economy on Thursday, sharply contrasting expressions of anxiety and frustration from scores of smaller businesses grappling with the fresh reality of a full-blown trade war with the United States.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Footage of Tibet floods isn't being shown in China - and we know little about victims there
candidates.description: Some of the most dramatic footage from the deadly flash flooding is hidden from public view in China.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Norway's new king remembers 'my dear father' in first speech
candidates.description: Haakon VIII pays emotional tribute to his late father, Harald V, before outlining how he wishes to reign.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Landlady to 9/11 hijackers reveals their links to alleged Saudi spy
candidates.description: A woman who rented out homes to two al-Qaeda members speaks publicly for the first time - to the BBC.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Close race as Iceland votes on whether to restart talks on joining EU
candidates.description: Turbulent international affairs have brought the vote forward, but the campaign has focused more on Iceland's vital fishing industry.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Ex-White House teleprompter operator ordered to pay $172,000 for Trump speech bets
candidates.description: The staffer was found to have used his prior knowledge of the president's speeches to place lucrative bets.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Russia ramps up rhetoric but wants to avoid war with Nato, Western officials say
candidates.description: But they say Moscow will likely continue its "hybrid activity" against Nato members, short of direct military action.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Berlin is being blackmailed by hackers, mayor says
candidates.description: Kai Wegner says the German capital and city-state would not cave in to a ransom demand for data stolen in a cyber-attack.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Thieves steal 600-diamond necklace from Vienna museum in broad daylight
candidates.description: Police are hunting two suspects they believe bought a ticket for the exhibition to get at the jewellery.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Violence breaks out in Ceuta as migrant crisis continues
candidates.description: A group of migrants is accused of throwing stones at a military vehicle, while some locals set fire to their camps on the beach.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: US plans to cut off military aid to key Middle East ally, BBC told
candidates.description: Iraqi Kurdistan fears the Trump administration's plan will make the region more vulnerable to further attacks from Iran.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Shootings surge as drug gangs torment Brussels
candidates.description: This year alone there have been more than 65 shootings in the Belgian capital, as drug crime soars.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Australia usually hosts the world's biggest cuttlefish mating event - not this year
candidates.description: According to official figures only 1,811 cuttlefish turned up to mate this year, down 97% on last year.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Somali piracy surges as the impact of the US-Iran war ripples outwards
candidates.description: Two ships were seized within four days last week raising to at least 13 the number attacked since January.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: What tariffs will really cost Canadians and Americans
candidates.description: Households and businesses have become used to tariffs impacting the cost of living for more than year now, so what will change now?
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Norway's King Harald dies aged 89: A beloved monarch buffeted by family crises
candidates.description: The late king, who reigned for 35 years, broke with tradition by marrying a commoner and was widely loved by Norwegians.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Deadly strike on Kyiv warehouse prompts evacuations
candidates.description: Ukraine correspondent Dan Johnson reports from Kyiv after the deadly strike, which authorities said killed more than 30 people.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: BBC tracks one week of Israeli settler violence in occupied West Bank
candidates.description: The BBC's Lucy Williamson reports on settler attacks on Palestinians, which have been observed over the last week alone.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Watch: Why rescuers fear new barrier lake could cause another Nepal-Tibet flood
candidates.description: Laura Bicker explains how a lake which formed after the recent landslide near the Nepal-Tibet border is raising fears of a second flood.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Watch: Stargazers around the world glimpse 'Blood Moon' lunar eclipse
candidates.description: Some parts of the globe had a chance to see the rare event when the Sun, Earth and Moon line up in the night sky.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Matt Lucas and Hugh Bonneville among actors calling for law on AI voice cloning
candidates.description: The performers are asking the government to give every person in the UK a legal right to own their voice.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Strong winds and thunderstorms kick off the bank holiday weekend
candidates.description: Cooler and showery conditions will continue across the weekend and into Monday, bringing a record-breaking summer to a rather damp close as Matt Taylor explains.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: How the weather in space can affect us on Earth - and the team trying to protect us
candidates.description: The weather in space has the potential to impact our lives here on Earth in a fundamental way.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: 'Our parents were crossing the border an hour before the flood hit'
candidates.description: Authorities say nearly 2,000 people are missing, including more than 100 Americans and Canadians, as families await word on loved ones after the Nepal flash floods.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Bank holiday weekend to see more thunderstorms and rain
candidates.description: The weather will remain unsettled across the next few days with showers, longer spells of rain and thunderstorms all likely at times across the weekend.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Russian strike near Kyiv kills 37, in one of the year's deadliest attacks
candidates.description: The deadly strike comes amid 72 hours of near constant drone strikes across Ukraine, severely disrupting daily life.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Photos: See the aftermath of deadly flash floods in Nepal
candidates.description: Nepal officials say the death toll has continues to rise in Wednesday's floods that washed away communities in Nepal and Tibet, which is held by China. About 2,500 people are missing in both areas.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Srebrenica survivor Ahmed Hrustanovic reflects on Ratko Mladic's death
candidates.description: Ahmed Hrustanovic reflects on Ratko Mladic's death with NPR's Scott Simon. All of Hrustanovic's adult male relatives died in the Srebrenica Massacre engineered by Mladic.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Trump says U.S. has entered deal with Venezuela to take control of 65 billion barrels of oil reserves
candidates.description: President Trump says his administration has entered a sweeping agreement with Venezuela that could give the U.S. access to vast amounts of the South American country's untapped oil reserves, at cost.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Experts warn more flooding might hit Nepal. And, Fed chairman to give key address
candidates.description: As the death toll rises from flash floods that hit the Nepal-Tibet border, experts are warning more flooding could be on the way. And, Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh is expected to give a key address today.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Hundreds killed, over 1,000 missing after flash floods in Nepal and Tibet
candidates.description: Hundreds of people were killed by devastating flash floods that hit the Nepal-Tibet border, sweeping away roads, bridges and entire villages. More than 1,000 people are still missing.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: 'It's essentially been one long day': A daughter details search for parents in Nepal
candidates.description: Shreya Ahuja is searching for her parents after devastating floods struck Nepal. She is calling for international help and communications access as her family waits for news.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: U.S. says pipelines will make Strait of Hormuz irrelevant. Energy experts disagree
candidates.description: Treasure Secretary Scott Bessent said oil pipelines will make Strait of Hormuz irrelevant in two years. Energy experts say that is unlikely to happen.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: A melting glacier contributed to the deadly Nepal floods. We can expect more like this
candidates.description: As the climate continues to warm, scientists warn that the frequency of disasters like the floods in Nepal will increase.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Social media restrictions on young users: What do the kids say?
candidates.description: We've heard from adults about the new Facebook and Instagram rules, but what are kids saying? Teenage social media users talk about whether the proposed restrictions will have any effect on them.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Fed's Kevin Warsh warns inflation is too high, sparking bets rate hikes are coming
candidates.description: Fed Chair Kevin Warsh reiterated his commitment to fighting inflation in a major speech — raising expectations that rate hikes may be coming, though he did not clearly spell out a path going forward.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Businesses are getting tariff refunds. Why aren't consumers getting their cut?
candidates.description: A slew of American companies are getting billions of dollars back in tariff refunds after a Supreme Court ruling. Many consumers, though, may never get anything back.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: The bridges of Rwanda open up new worlds
candidates.description: A charity built 96 bridges to connect communities separated by rivers and gorges. A new study looks at the life-changing impact of a concrete-and-steel pedestrian crossing.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Pennsylvania measles deaths ignite clash over RFK Jr.'s vaccination claims
candidates.description: Two deaths associated with the measles outbreak in Pennsylvania prompted messaging from the health secretary that both encouraged and undermined vaccinations.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Lights out, Instagram off? The changes to Meta for teens could be a big deal
candidates.description: Researchers and advocates are applauding the changes that Meta agreed to make for minors on Instagram and Facebook. Cutting kids off at night and during the school day are two big changes.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Trump cuts to science advisory boards have long-lasting consequences, researchers say
candidates.description: The federal government recruits top experts to volunteer to advise on pressing research issues of the day. Since President Trump took office, hundreds of these experts have been dismissed.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: 4 ways to cope with constant thoughts about your body image
candidates.description: Obsessing over your looks should not take up all your energy, says psychologist Diana Hill. If you're struggling with uncomfortable thoughts about your body, ground yourself with these techniques.
candidates.author: NPR
